summary.intent: Complete a /simplify review pass on Phase 24 code, fix resulting issues, and get a PR up for the changes.
summary.outcome: All simplification and type fixes were committed, PR #361 was created, and a CI build failure from the refactor was diagnosed and patched.

repo: TypeScript does not propagate type narrowing across function call boundaries — a helper like validateRegistryShape() that checks Array.isArray() does not narrow the type for the caller.
Packages @cipherbox/crypto and @cipherbox/api-client must be explicitly rebuilt to regenerate .d.ts files; stale builds cause downstream web app type errors.
The project uses a phase-based development model (e.g., Phase 24) with structured commit conventions like refactor(24): and fix(load):

code.finding: After extracting validateRegistryShape() to deduplicate v1/v2 validation, obj.devices remained type 'unknown' at the call site because TS18046 narrowing doesn't cross function boundaries. Fixed with a cast after validation.
validateRegistryShape() was introduced as a deduplication helper for v1/v2 registry validation logic.

workflow: CI failures on a branch may not appear immediately — gh run list may show passing runs first; filtering by status is needed to find failures.
Rebuilding dependent packages before running type checks prevents false-positive type errors from stale .d.ts files.

friction: CI build failed after the /simplify refactor due to a TypeScript narrowing limitation across function boundaries — the fix required a follow-up commit after the PR was already created.
Stale package builds (.d.ts files) caused 6 type errors in the web app that were not immediately attributable to the current changes.
